items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...listening to Let's Talk It Over with your moderator, Joseph Collada.

ctx.x: I mean, I'm scared of graveyards. Well, I've heard that recording, and I would assume that Papa Salastain, of course, was telling the truth. Of course, these things happen many times. Somebody may have asked thus and such a musician or thus and such a musician to do a similar thing, and he thinks he's the first one. It's awful hard to prove something like that. Things get invented simultaneously. You'll find that true in the theory of evolution. Right. You study any subject, and you'll find the origins of it are…
This is WTIS 690 in New Orleans, Louisiana, and you are listening to Let's Talk It Over with your moderator, Joseph Collada.

Okay, back in tune with more of Let's Talk It Over. We have, well, not a lot of time to play all of the records that Dick Allen had selected this morning. I knew this was going to happen. I asked them to choose some. I'm going to ask if we can jump over Snoozer Quinn now. I want to go back to Johnny Wiggs and the New Orleans Kings, because this is a great song. Congo Square. You know, that has a bit of a tear in it. I can picture somebody sitting around the waterfront at about 3 o'clock on a Sunday morning, you…
